transcript.raw_output: {"type":" "say", "text": "Good morning, everyone. We need to get the wrap disposition plan locked today so we're ready for Friday's set dismantling. Per our standard wrap process, I need each department lead to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for their area. If anyone has an exception to the current draft — scenic pieces going to general salvage, selected hero props going to production storage — I need you to state the exact corrective requirement now so it can be entered into the meeting record before I can approve the plan. Let's start with the first department. Who wants to go first?"}

transcript.text: I need to flag an exception on the wrap plan: the antique jukebox is a rented hero prop. I confirmed with the rental house yesterday that its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition — it cannot go into production storage or salvage. This hasn't been entered in the wrap packet yet, so I need it on the record before we lock the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an exception on the wrap plan from a sustainability and compliance standpoint. The city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. I confirmed with the vendor this morning that the approved vendor's audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. However, the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft, not the audited plan. This needs to be corrected and entered into the meeting record before the plan is locked.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text:
Thank you both for flagging these exceptions. Both are valid and need to be entered into the meeting record before I can approve the plan.

Derek, I'm noting your exception: the antique jukebox is a rented hero prop with a rental agreement requiring return to the owner in original condition — it cannot go to production storage or salvage. The corrective requirement is to remove it from the production storage list and route it back to the rental house per the agreement.

Lina, I'm noting your exception: the city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill, and the approved vendor's audited plan only meets that threshold through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. The compliance packet currently contains the general-salvage draft, not the audited plan. The corrective requirement is to replace the general-salvage draft with the vendor's audited diversion plan and include the certified transfer record.

Once both of these exceptions are formally entered into the meeting record, I'll be in a position to approve the corrected wrap disposition plan. Can both of you confirm your exception statements are accurate and complete as I've read them back, so we can get them entered?
